findings.description: New comment justifying the feat/x checkout gets git-safety.sh's rule order backwards: it claims staying on trunk would let the branch rule block the push first, masking the force-push rule, but the force-push check (line 142) exits the script via block() before CURRENT_BRANCH is even computed (line 153) or the trunk check runs (line 167) - so the force-push rule always fires first for `git push --force origin main` regardless of which branch the temp repo is on.
findings.body:
The new comment reads:
```
// On the trunk a push is blocked by the branch rule too, so the assertion below would pass
// without the force-push rule it names ever being reached.
```
This gets the control flow in `templates/agents/hooks/policies/git-safety.sh` backwards. The force-push check runs first and exits unconditionally:
```sh
if printf '%s' "$PUSHES" | grep -qE -- '(^|[[:space:]])(--force|-f)([[:space:]]|$)'; then
  block 'force push. Push normally, or ask the user.'
fi
...
CURRENT_BRANCH=$(git -C "${AGENT_CWD:-$PROJECT_DIR}" branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || echo '')
...
if [ "$CURRENT_BRANCH" = "$TRUNK" ]; then
  ...
fi
```
`block()` calls `exit 2` directly (not inside a subshell), so it terminates the script before `CURRENT_BRANCH` is computed or the trunk/branch rule at the bottom of the file runs. For the test's exact command (`git push --force origin main`), the force-push rule always fires first and the branch/trunk rule is never reached, whether the temp repo is on `main` or `feat/x`. The checkout to `feat/x` therefore has no bearing on which rule the test's push trips - the comment's stated reasoning for it doesn't hold. This is a factually incorrect WHY comment (AGENTS.md's Comments rule requires the WHY to be true, not just present), and it reintroduces the original ambiguity the comment was added to resolve (why does this checkout exist), just with a wrong answer instead of no answer.
